# 📚 Pagewise

**Chat with your PDFs.** Pagewise is a Streamlit app that lets you upload one or more PDF files and ask questions about them in a chat interface. Answers are generated by Google Gemini using Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG), and every answer comes with the **file name and page number** of the sources it used.

Each user has their own account, so uploaded documents and chat history are saved privately and restored the next time you log in.

## Features

- **Chat with multiple PDFs** at once
- **Page-level citations**: every answer lists the source file and page (`report.pdf (p. 4)`)
- **Balanced retrieval across files**: when several PDFs are loaded, chunks are retrieved from each file separately so no document gets drowned out
- **Follow-up questions**: recent conversation history is used to resolve context
- **User accounts**: sign up / log in with username and password (salted PBKDF2-SHA256 hashing, no plaintext passwords)
- **Per-user persistence**: your FAISS index, file list, and chat history are saved and restored on login
- **Free-tier friendly**: embeddings are batched and throttled, with automatic wait-and-retry on rate limit (HTTP 429) errors
- **Clear feedback**: warns about scanned/image-only PDFs with no extractable text

---

## How it works

```
PDFs ──► extract text per page ──► split into chunks (1500 chars, 200 overlap)
     ──► Gemini embeddings ──► FAISS vector store (saved per user)

Question ──► retrieve top chunks (MMR for 1 file, per-file search for many)
         ──► prompt + history + context ──► Gemini ──► answer + sources
```

1. **Ingestion**: each PDF page is read with PyPDF2 and split separately, so every chunk keeps `{source, page}` metadata.
2. **Embedding**: chunks are embedded with `models/gemini-embedding-001` in throttled batches and stored in a FAISS index.
3. **Retrieval**: for a single file, Maximal Marginal Relevance (MMR) search returns diverse chunks. For multiple files, the top chunks are fetched from each file.
4. **Answering**: the retrieved context and recent chat history are passed to a Gemini chat model through a LangChain (LCEL) chain. The model is instructed to answer only from the documents and to reply *"Answer is not available in the context."* when the answer isn't there.

---

## Tech stack

- [Streamlit](https://streamlit.io/): UI
- [LangChain](https://www.langchain.com/): chains, prompts, text splitting
- [Google Gemini](https://ai.google.dev/) via `langchain-google-genai`: chat model and embeddings
- [FAISS](https://github.com/facebookresearch/faiss): vector search
- [PyPDF2](https://pypi.org/project/PyPDF2/): PDF text extraction
- SQLite: user accounts

## Getting started

### Prerequisites

- Python 3.9+
- A Google Gemini API key: get one free at [Google AI Studio](https://aistudio.google.com/app/apikey)

### Installation

```bash
# 1. Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/<your-username>/<your-repo>.git
cd <your-repo>

# 2. Create and activate a virtual environment
python -m venv venv
source venv/bin/activate        # Windows: venv\Scripts\activate

# 3. Install dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

### Configuration

Create a `.env` file in the project root:

```env
GOOGLE_API_KEY=your_gemini_api_key_here

# Optional: override the default chat model
# GEMINI_MODEL=gemini-2.5-flash

# Optional: custom location for the users database (default: users.db)
# USERS_DB=users.db
```

> ⚠️ Never commit your `.env` file. It is already listed in `.gitignore`.

### Run the app

```bash
streamlit run app.py
```

Then open the URL shown in the terminal (usually http://localhost:8501).

---

## Usage

1. **Sign up** for an account, then **log in**.
2. In the sidebar, upload one or more PDF files.
3. Click **Submit & Process** and wait for embedding to finish.
4. Ask questions in the chat box. Expand **Sources** under any answer to see the file and pages used.
5. Use **Clear chat** to reset the conversation, or **Log out** when you're done. Your documents stay saved for next time.

---

## Project structure

```
.
├── app.py             # Streamlit app: PDF processing, retrieval, chat UI
├── auth.py            # Username/password auth backed by SQLite
├── requirements.txt   # Python dependencies
├── .gitignore
├── users.db           # (generated) user accounts, git-ignored
└── data/              # (generated) per-user FAISS index + chat history, git-ignored
    └── users/<username>/
        ├── index/
        ├── files.json
        └── messages.json
```

---

## Configuration reference

| Setting | Where | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `GOOGLE_API_KEY` | `.env` | none (required) | Gemini API key |
| `GEMINI_MODEL` | `.env` | set in `app.py` | Gemini chat model name |
| `USERS_DB` | `.env` | `users.db` | SQLite file for user accounts |
| `CHUNK_SIZE` / `CHUNK_OVERLAP` | `app.py` | 1500 / 200 | Text splitting |
| `TOTAL_K` | `app.py` | 8 | Chunks sent to the model per question |
| `EMBED_BATCH` / `EMBED_INTERVAL` | `app.py` | 40 / 30s | Embedding throttle for free-tier limits |
| `HISTORY_TURNS` | `app.py` | 6 | Past messages used for follow-ups |

---

## Limitations

- **Scanned PDFs** (images without a text layer) are not supported, since there is no OCR.
- The Gemini free tier has strict rate limits, so large PDFs can take a while to embed.
- Authentication is intentionally simple (no email verification or password reset). Add a stronger solution before any public deployment.
